detail.longDescription: Harnessing The Machine Learning Algorithm For Landslide Susceptibility Mapping In A Mountainous Road Corridors Of NH-2 And NH-29, Nagaland [India] -- https:// doi.org/10.1007/s44288-026-008 28-4 <-- shared paper -- H/T @ dr . Jayanta Das | Assistant Professor at Department of Geography, Rampurhat College, Scientific Editor, Next Research, Elsevier, Director, Srushti-Drushti Geospatial (SDG) Foundation (NGO) “🔍 Research Highlights: • Comparative assessment of six advanced machine learning algorithms: Random Forest, Deep Neural Network, SVM, Gradient Boosting Machine, MLP and XGBoost. • Identification and analysis of 463 landslide locations using field surveys, satellite imagery and the Bhukosh database. • Integration of GIS, remote sensing, Boruta feature selection and Getis-Ord Gi* hotspot analysis. - SVM achieved a prediction accuracy of 93.2% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.812. • Identification of highly susceptible locations along NH-2 and NH-29, including Tuli, Lumami-Zunheboto, Kohima and Medziphema. The findings provide valuable insights for landslide hazard assessment, infrastructure planning, community-based mitigation and disaster risk reduction in the fragile mountainous environment of Northeast India…” # LandslideSusceptibility # MachineLearning # model # modelling # prediction # algorithms # assessment # AI # GIS # RemoteSensing # GeospatialTechnology # DisasterRiskReduction # Nagaland # NortheastIndia # SpringerNature # DiscoverGeoscience # massmovement # landslide # spatialanalysis # spatiotemporal # literaturereview # remotesensing # GIS # spatial # mapping # engineeringgeology # geology # geomorphology # risk # hazard # infrastructure # cost # damage # economics # hazardassessment # mitigation # naturalhazard # disaster # riskreduction # mountain # slope # elevation # montane # India # Nagaland # Dimapur # Kohima # Wokha # Mokokchung # Changtongya # Tuli
